title: How to Fix the Instagram Messaging API Error
html:
How to Fix the Instagram Messaging API Error

Updated Sep 9, 2026

If you’re trying to connect your Instagram account to LinktoDM and see the message “Instagram Business API: Your Instagram account is ineligible for using Instagram Business Messaging API,” this guide will help you fix it.

First, which way did you connect?

Section titled “First, which way did you connect?”

The eligibility rules are different on the two connection routes, and most wasted time on this error comes from working through the wrong list. LinktoDM offers:

  • Instagram login — you sign in with your Instagram credentials. No Facebook involved at any point.
  • Facebook login — you sign in with Facebook and connect a Page. The Page carries the permissions.

Why a Facebook Page is required explains the difference in full. Pick your route below.

If you connected with Instagram login

Section titled “If you connected with Instagram login”

There is exactly one requirement, and no Facebook Page or Business Manager is involved.

Your Instagram account must be professional. Business and Creator both work — Meta exposes messaging on either. A personal account cannot be automated by LinktoDM or by any other tool, because Meta doesn’t expose the messaging permissions on it at all. See why a professional account is required.

To see which type you’re on, open Creator tools and controls under For professionals in Instagram’s settings. That entry is named after the type you’re currently on, and the panel lists the types you can move to.

Switching a personal account to professional is free, takes about a minute, and doesn’t change your handle, followers or posts.

Then check the messaging switch, which a switch of account type resets:

  • Switch Allow access to messages on. It lives in the Instagram mobile app, not on the web — Fix DM access disabled has the steps and covers this one on its own.

You do not need a Facebook account, a Facebook Page, or a Meta Business portfolio on this route. If a checklist somewhere told you otherwise, it was describing the Facebook route.

If you connected with Facebook login

Section titled “If you connected with Facebook login”

Here the Facebook Page is the object Meta attaches permissions to, so the Page requirements come first.

  1. You must administer a Facebook Page. Being able to post to a Page is not the same as being an admin of it — without the admin role there is nobody Meta will accept the permission grant from. A Page on its own is a complete setup for Messenger DMs and comment-to-DM on Facebook posts.
  2. For the Instagram features, link an Instagram professional account to that Page. The linkage is made from Instagram’s professional account settings, or from the Page’s own Linked accounts settings on Facebook. An Instagram account with no linked Page cannot use this route — that’s the one thing the Page is genuinely required for.
  3. Add both the Page and the Instagram account to the same Meta Business portfolio. Meta Business Settings → Accounts → add them under Pages and Instagram accounts. Both in the same portfolio; split across two is a common cause of this error.
  4. Turn message access on. The Allow access to messages switch is in the Instagram mobile app — Fix DM access disabled.

After you change anything

Section titled “After you change anything”

Meta doesn’t propagate these changes instantly. Give it a while — often under an hour, sometimes several — then connect to LinktoDM again. Reconnecting repeatedly in the meantime doesn’t speed it up.

Then comment your trigger word from a second account and confirm both the public reply and the DM arrive.

App Review isn’t your side

This error is sometimes attributed to the Meta app’s Instagram Messaging permissions not being approved. That approval belongs to LinktoDM’s Meta app, not to your account — it’s already in place, and there is nothing for you to configure. If everything above checks out, the problem is elsewhere.

Still not working?

Section titled “Still not working?”

Work through it in this order:

  1. Confirm the account is professional (Business or Creator), not personal.
  2. Confirm Allow access to messages is on.
  3. On the Facebook route only, confirm the Page and the Instagram account are in the same Business portfolio and that you’re a Page admin.
  4. Refresh permissions from scratch — Instagram automation not working.

If it survives all four, contact support@linktodm.com with your Instagram username, which route you connected on, and the time you last tried.

You do not need a Facebook account, a Facebook Page, or a Meta Business portfolio on this route. If a checklist somewhere told you otherwise, it was describing the Facebook route.

If you connected with Facebook login
Section titled “If you connected with Facebook login”

Here the Facebook Page is the object Meta attaches permissions to, so the Page requirements come first.

You must administer a Facebook Page. Being able to post to a Page is not the same as being an admin of it — without the admin role there is nobody Meta will accept the permission grant from. A Page on its own is a complete setup for Messenger DMs and comment-to-DM on Facebook posts.
For the Instagram features, link an Instagram professional account to that Page. The linkage is made from Instagram’s professional account settings, or from the Page’s own Linked accounts settings on Facebook. An Instagram account with no linked Page cannot use this route — that’s the one thing the Page is genuinely required for.
Add both the Page and the Instagram account to the same Meta Business portfolio. Meta Business Settings → Accounts → add them under Pages and Instagram accounts. Both in the same portfolio; split across two is a common cause of this error.
Turn message access on. The Allow access to messages switch is in the Instagram mobile app — Fix DM access disabled.
After you change anything
Section titled “After you change anything”

Meta doesn’t propagate these changes instantly. Give it a while — often under an hour, sometimes several — then connect to LinktoDM again. Reconnecting repeatedly in the meantime doesn’t speed it up.

Then comment your trigger word from a second account and confirm both the public reply and the DM arrive.

App Review isn’t your side

This error is sometimes attributed to the Meta app’s Instagram Messaging permissions not being approved. That approval belongs to LinktoDM’s Meta app, not to your account — it’s already in place, and there is nothing for you to configure. If everything above checks out, the problem is elsewhere.

Still not working?
Section titled “Still not working?”

Work through it in this order:

Confirm the account is professional (Business or Creator), not personal.
Confirm Allow access to messages is on.
On the Facebook route only, confirm the Page and the Instagram account are in the same Business portfolio and that you’re a Page admin.
Refresh permissions from scratch — Instagram automation not working.

title: Fix 'The Account Owner Has Disabled Access to Instagram Direct Messages'
html:
Fix 'The Account Owner Has Disabled Access to Instagram Direct Messages'

Updated Sep 9, 2026

“The account owner has disabled access to Instagram direct messages” is one of the tidier Instagram errors, because it names exactly what’s wrong and there’s a single switch behind it.

Your Instagram account has Allow access to messages turned off. That switch governs whether any third-party tool may read or send your DMs. With it off, LinktoDM’s connection is otherwise healthy — permissions granted, account eligible, automations published — and every message still fails.

Turn message access back on

Section titled “Turn message access back on”

The setting lives in the Instagram mobile app, not on the web.

  1. Open Instagram and go to Settings and activity.
  2. Tap Messages and story replies (on some versions: Privacy → Messages).
  3. Find Connected tools and open it.
  4. Switch Allow access to messages on.

Instagram sometimes takes a little while to propagate the change to connected apps. If automations are still failing after a few minutes, force the update from the LinktoDM side:

  1. Log out of LinktoDM.
  2. Log back in and reconnect Instagram, approving every permission — Connect your Instagram account has the flow.

Then comment your trigger word from a second account and confirm the DM arrives.

Why it switches itself off

Section titled “Why it switches itself off”

You probably didn’t turn it off deliberately. Three things flip it:

  • A password change or a security checkpoint. Instagram revokes third-party message access when it re-secures an account — see Reconnect Instagram after a password change.
  • Switching the account type back to Personal and then to Professional again. The switch resets to off.
  • Removing and re-adding an app without approving the messaging permission on the way through.

Not the same as removing the app

This switch is separate from the LinktoDM entry in Apps and websites. An account can show LinktoDM as connected and still have message access off — which is why the automation looks fine in the dashboard right up until it tries to send. If you’ve already reconnected once and the error persists, this switch is the thing you haven’t checked.

Still failing after switching it on

Section titled “Still failing after switching it on”

If the error survives both the setting and a reconnection, the account may be carrying a restriction rather than a setting. Check the Messaging API eligibility list, then contact support@linktodm.com with your username and the time of a failed send.

title: How to Fix Another App Controlling Your Instagram Conversations
html:
How to Fix Another App Controlling Your Instagram Conversations

Updated Sep 9, 2026

If you recently switched to LinktoDM from another tool like ManyChat, or any other Instagram/Facebook messaging app, you may see an error like “the action is invalid since it’s not the thread owner” when trying to send a reply. This guide explains what’s happening and how to fix it.

Why this happens

Section titled “Why this happens”

Instagram and Facebook only allow one app at a time to send messages on a given conversation. This is part of Meta’s Handover Protocol (also called Conversation Routing). When you previously connected another app like ManyChat, that app became the “thread owner” for your conversations. Until that other app is disconnected, LinktoDM is held in standby and cannot send replies, even though the connection itself is healthy.

Important: remove the other app from both Facebook and Instagram

Section titled “Important: remove the other app from both Facebook and Instagram”

It does not matter whether you signed in to LinktoDM with Instagram Login or with a Facebook Page. Apps like ManyChat are usually connected on both sides: your Meta Business portfolio and your Instagram account. Removing it from only one place is not enough; the other side will keep claiming thread ownership and the error will come back. Please complete both sets of steps below.

Step 1: Remove the app from Meta Business Suite (Facebook side)

Section titled “Step 1: Remove the app from Meta Business Suite (Facebook side)”
  1. Open Meta Business Suite → Settings and select your business portfolio at the top.
  2. In the left sidebar, expand Integrations and click Connected apps.
  3. Click the other app (for example Manychat) in the Connected tab, then click the Remove button on the top-right of the panel.
  4. Confirm the removal when Meta asks. The app will move from Connected to the Removed tab.

Step 2: Remove the app from Instagram

Section titled “Step 2: Remove the app from Instagram”
  1. On a desktop browser, log in to the same Instagram account you connected to LinktoDM and open Instagram → Apps and Websites.
  2. Switch to the Active tab and find the other app in the list.
  3. Click Remove next to it and confirm. The app will move to the Expired or Removed list.
  4. On the Instagram mobile app, you can do the same from Settings and activity → App website permissions → Apps and websites.

Step 3: Wait a few minutes, then verify

Section titled “Step 3: Wait a few minutes, then verify”
  • Wait a few minutes after removing the app from both places. Meta needs time to release thread ownership across all your existing conversations.
  • Refresh your LinktoDM dashboard. The amber warning banner should disappear automatically.
  • Send a test reply to an existing conversation from your Inbox. It should succeed without an error toast.
  • Automations (comment-to-DM, story replies, etc.) should resume sending messages on new conversations.

Still seeing the error?

Section titled “Still seeing the error?”

A few older conversations may stay assigned to the previous app even after you remove it. Ask the other person to send you a new message. Meta will reassign that thread to LinktoDM automatically. If the warning is still there well after you’ve removed the other app from both Facebook and Instagram, please contact our support team with screenshots of your Meta Business → Connected apps page and your Instagram Apps and Websites page so we can help.

title: Reconnect Instagram After a Password Change
html:
Reconnect Instagram After a Password Change

Updated Sep 9, 2026

Everything worked yesterday. You changed your Instagram password — or cleared a security checkpoint, or Meta prompted you to re-secure the account — and today nothing fires.

Instagram invalidates the access token when the password changes. “Error validating access token: the session has been invalidated” is Meta telling you the connection LinktoDM holds is no longer valid. The automations themselves are untouched; they simply have no permission to run.

It fails silently. There’s no email and no banner from Instagram — the first sign is usually a quiet day, which is why this one often goes unnoticed for a week.

Reconnect

Section titled “Reconnect”
  1. Log out of LinktoDM.
  2. Log back in and choose the same connection method you used originally — Instagram login or Facebook login. Switching methods here creates a second connection rather than repairing the first.
  3. Approve every permission Meta asks for. A partially approved reconnection looks successful and then fails at the first send.
  4. Publish nothing new — your existing automations resume on the restored connection.

Connect your Instagram account has the full flow if you need the screenshots.

Check these two afterwards

Section titled “Check these two afterwards”

A password change often takes more than the token with it.

Message access. Instagram frequently resets Allow access to messages to off when it re-secures an account. Comment automations may look fine while every DM fails — fix DM access disabled.

The queue. Anything that was waiting to send while the token was dead is still there. Open the In queue panel: if the count is high and the messages are now stale, clearing the queue is kinder than delivering a two-day-old reply to someone who’s forgotten they commented.

Then test

Section titled “Then test”

Comment your trigger word from a second account and confirm the whole chain runs — public reply and DM. A token restored without message access will pass the first half of that test and fail the second, which is exactly the state that sends people back to square one.

Every connected account needs this

Tokens are per Instagram account. If you run several connected accounts and changed the password on one, only that one needs reconnecting — but check the others’ automations are still running before you assume so.

title: Public Comment Replies Temporarily Restricted
html:
Public Comment Replies Temporarily Restricted

Updated Sep 9, 2026

Your DMs are going out but the public replies under comments have stopped, or Instagram is returning “based on previous use of this feature”.

This is Instagram’s anti-spam system, and it’s account-level rather than automation-level. Something about the volume, speed or sameness of your replies crossed a threshold, and Instagram has paused that ability for a while.

What sets it off

Section titled “What sets it off”

Four things, usually in combination:

  • Volume in a short window. A post that takes off produces hundreds of qualifying comments in minutes, and every one gets a public reply.
  • Identical text. A hundred comments answered with the exact same sentence is the clearest possible spam signature.
  • Links in public replies. A URL repeated under every comment attracts attention far faster than plain text.
  • A young or recently reconnected account. New professional accounts have less headroom than established ones.

What to do now

Section titled “What to do now”

Stop replying while it’s restricted. Switch the automation’s public reply off — or pause the automation — for a day or two. Continuing to push against a restriction extends it; that’s the whole design.

The DM half can keep running. Public replies and private replies are separate capabilities, so disabling the public reply while you wait doesn’t stop the automation delivering.

Restrictions are temporary and lift on their own. There is no appeal, no support ticket that shortens it, and no setting that raises the limit.

Preventing the next one

Section titled “Preventing the next one”

Cap the replies. Set a reply limit on the automation so it stops after a set number instead of running unbounded on a post that unexpectedly performs. This is the single most effective control.

Never send the same sentence twice. Write several public replies and let them rotate, or use AI public replies so every reply is a fresh sentence. Rotation is not cosmetic here — it’s the difference between looking like a person and looking like a script.

Keep links out of the public reply. Put the URL in the DM, where it belongs and where it converts better anyway. “Sent you a DM 📩” is a better public reply than a link.

Don’t backtrack a big post in one go. Backtracking a week of comments creates the exact volume spike this restriction watches for.

Different from the DM rate limit

Instagram limits private replies to 750 per hour and LinktoDM’s queue absorbs that automatically. Public replies are governed by a separate, unpublished anti-spam system that blocks rather than throttles — which is why the queue can’t smooth it out for you. See rate limits and throttling.

title: DMs Are Very Slow to Arrive
html:
DMs Are Very Slow to Arrive

Updated Sep 9, 2026

Slow delivery is usually the system working, not failing. Before treating it as a fault, it’s worth knowing which of the two you’re looking at.

First, read the queue

Section titled “First, read the queue”

Open the In queue panel in the console. It shows how many DMs and follow-ups are waiting and the rate they’re going out at — check your DM queue status explains how to read it.

What the panel shows What it means
A high count that’s falling Working through a spike. Leave it
A count that’s flat or rising for hours Arrivals are outpacing sending — see below
Zero waiting, but DMs still slow Not a queue problem. Skip to the last section

Why the queue slows down deliberately

Section titled “Why the queue slows down deliberately”

Instagram caps private replies at 750 per hour per professional account, and caps overall API activity on a 24-hour rolling budget scaled by your impressions. A post that produces two thousand qualifying comments in an hour is over that line no matter how the sending is spaced.

LinktoDM’s Smart Queue Control watches how Instagram responds and eases off when it sees rate limiting, then picks the pace back up. A queue that drains slowly during a spike is the system choosing delivery over speed: the messages still arrive, later than they would have. Pushing harder gets them rejected instead.

There is no setting to raise the rate, no priority lane, and no plan that buys more of it — the limits are Instagram’s and apply to every tool. Rate limits and throttling has the full picture.

When a large queue is a problem

Section titled “When a large queue is a problem”

It’s stale. Messages queued during a spike keep their place, but a DM answering a comment from six hours ago can land oddly. If the backlog has passed the point of being useful, clear the queue rather than delivering it — and switch the automation off first, or it refills.

It never drains. A count that’s been flat for hours with nothing going out usually isn’t throttling — it’s a broken connection. Check permissions, a password change, and message access.

You backtracked a big post. Backtracking a week of comments dumps the lot into the queue at once, against the same hourly ceiling as live traffic. Expect hours, and expect it to compete with new comments arriving.

When the queue is empty and DMs are still slow

Section titled “When the queue is empty and DMs are still slow”

The delay isn’t in sending, so look at the automation itself:

  • A delay step you set and forgot — check the automation for one before assuming a fault.
  • A follow-up waiting on a condition. Follow-ups are counted separately from DMs in the queue panel for exactly this reason.
  • An opener message — the real content doesn’t send until the recipient taps the button, so “slow” here is the recipient, not the system.
  • It arrived on time, in Message requests, and was seen hours later.

text:
DMs Are Very Slow to Arrive

Updated Sep 9, 2026

Slow delivery is usually the system working, not failing. Before treating it as a fault, it’s worth knowing which of the two you’re looking at.

First, read the queue
Section titled “First, read the queue”

Open the In queue panel in the console. It shows how many DMs and follow-ups are waiting and the rate they’re going out at — check your DM queue status explains how to read it.

Counts, current rate, and the two controls — the count and its direction are what matter here
WHAT THE PANEL SHOWS	WHAT IT MEANS
A high count that’s falling	Working through a spike. Leave it
A count that’s flat or rising for hours	Arrivals are outpacing sending — see below
Zero waiting, but DMs still slow	Not a queue problem. Skip to the last section
Why the queue slows down deliberately
Section titled “Why the queue slows down deliberately”

Instagram caps private replies at 750 per hour per professional account, and caps overall API activity on a 24-hour rolling budget scaled by your impressions. A post that produces two thousand qualifying comments in an hour is over that line no matter how the sending is spaced.

LinktoDM’s Smart Queue Control watches how Instagram responds and eases off when it sees rate limiting, then picks the pace back up. A queue that drains slowly during a spike is the system choosing delivery over speed: the messages still arrive, later than they would have. Pushing harder gets them rejected instead.

There is no setting to raise the rate, no priority lane, and no plan that buys more of it — the limits are Instagram’s and apply to every tool. Rate limits and throttling has the full picture.

When a large queue is a problem
Section titled “When a large queue is a problem”

It’s stale. Messages queued during a spike keep their place, but a DM answering a comment from six hours ago can land oddly. If the backlog has passed the point of being useful, clear the queue rather than delivering it — and switch the automation off first, or it refills.

It never drains. A count that’s been flat for hours with nothing going out usually isn’t throttling — it’s a broken connection. Check permissions, a password change, and message access.

You backtracked a big post. Backtracking a week of comments dumps the lot into the queue at once, against the same hourly ceiling as live traffic. Expect hours, and expect it to compete with new comments arriving.

When the queue is empty and DMs are still slow
Section titled “When the queue is empty and DMs are still slow”

The delay isn’t in sending, so look at the automation itself:

A delay step you set and forgot — check the automation for one before assuming a fault.
A follow-up waiting on a condition. Follow-ups are counted separately from DMs in the queue panel for exactly this reason.
An opener message — the real content doesn’t send until the recipient taps the button, so “slow” here is the recipient, not the system.
It arrived on time, in Message requests, and was seen hours later.

title: Links Aren't Clickable in an Automated DM
html:
Links Aren't Clickable in an Automated DM

Updated Sep 9, 2026

The DM arrives, the URL is in it, and it renders as plain text nobody can tap. This is Instagram’s rendering rather than a LinktoDM fault — but how you build the message decides how often it happens.

Use a button, not a bare URL

Section titled “Use a button, not a bare URL”

The most reliable way to deliver a link is a button. Buttons are a native message type: Instagram renders them as tappable controls, they aren’t subject to the app’s text link-detection, and they look deliberate rather than pasted.

Switch the message layout to text with buttons or an image card with buttons, give the button a label of up to 20 characters, and put the URL behind it. Buttons render and work on the Instagram mobile apps and on instagram.com in a desktop browser alike, so a button-only message is safe to send whatever your audience reads DMs on.

If you’re sending a bare URL

Section titled “If you’re sending a bare URL”

Put the URL on its own line, with a blank line above it. Instagram’s link-detection is more reliable when the URL isn’t wrapped in punctuation or buried mid-sentence. This is the single most effective fix for the Android app, which is markedly worse at detecting inline links than iOS.

Do this:

Not this:

Drop the trailing punctuation. A full stop or closing bracket immediately after a URL frequently gets absorbed into it, producing a link that 404s or doesn’t register at all.

Include the protocol. https://example.com detects reliably; example.com often doesn’t.

Avoid shorteners that look suspicious. Some redirect domains are treated warily. A custom domain or the real URL is safer.

If it’s not clickable for some people

Section titled “If it’s not clickable for some people”

They haven’t accepted the message request. A DM from an account someone doesn’t follow lands in Message requests, where the content is limited until they accept. Getting them to interact first is what fixes this, and that’s what an opener message is for: a greeting with a button, and the real link only after they’ve tapped. This solves link delivery and message-request burial in one move.

They’re on Android. See the blank-line fix above.

If links are blocked entirely

Section titled “If links are blocked entirely”

Instagram sometimes restricts an account from sending URLs. If every DM with a link fails while the same message without one goes through, that’s what’s happening. Send link-free messages for a day or two, keep the volume down, and let the restriction lapse. It’s the same anti-spam system described in public replies temporarily restricted.

title: Media Won't Send in an Automated DM
html:
Media Won't Send in an Automated DM

Updated Sep 9, 2026

The text part of the DM arrives and the attachment doesn’t, or the whole message fails. Instagram returns “upload attachment failure”, which covers everything from an oversized file to a format it won’t accept.

1. Check the file against the limits

Section titled “1. Check the file against the limits”

Most failures are here. The full media reference has the detail; the ceilings are:

Type Formats Max size
Image PNG, JPG, GIF 8 MB
Video MP4, MOV 25 MB
Audio AAC, M4A, WAV 25 MB
Document PDF 25 MB

GIFs go through as images, so they get the 8 MB ceiling, not 25 MB. A long loop exported as a GIF blows past it easily — export it as MP4 instead and it gets the video allowance.

Nothing else is accepted. WebP, HEIC, AVI, MKV, DOCX and ZIP will fail however small they are. Convert to a format on the list.

2. Re-upload the file

Section titled “2. Re-upload the file”

An upload that was interrupted leaves a media reference that looks fine in the editor and fails at send time. Remove the attachment, re-add it, and republish.

This is worth doing before anything else if the automation used to work and started failing without you changing it — media references don’t always survive account reconnection.

3. Compress rather than trim

Section titled “3. Compress rather than trim”

A 30 MB video isn’t a good DM attachment even if it fit. Under 25 MB is the hard limit, but well under it sends faster and fails less. Re-encode at a lower bitrate rather than cutting the content.

Images are the same story: an 8 MB PNG screenshot is usually a 400 KB JPG with no visible difference.

4. Check it’s not the rate limit

Section titled “4. Check it’s not the rate limit”

Instagram allows 10 DMs per second carrying audio or video, against 100 per second for text — media-heavy automations hit their ceiling ten times sooner. During a spike, media messages are the first to be throttled, so a video automation on a viral post will look slow and patchy while a text one alongside it runs fine. That’s the queue protecting the account, not a broken attachment.

5. Check the carousel

Section titled “5. Check the carousel”

Carousels cap at 10 cards, and every card needs its image, its title (80 characters) and its button label (20 characters). One incomplete card fails the whole message, and the card that’s missing something isn’t always the one you were editing last — check all of them.

Test the attachment on its own

Build a throwaway automation with nothing but the media, publish it, and trigger it from a second account. If it sends there and not in your real automation, the problem is elsewhere in the automation — not the file.

title: A Post Thumbnail Won't Load
html:
A Post Thumbnail Won't Load

Updated Sep 9, 2026

The post picker or the automation’s preview shows a grey box where the image should be. The good news first: this is almost always cosmetic. The automation is bound to the post’s ID, not its picture, so a missing thumbnail doesn’t stop anything from triggering.

Why thumbnails go blank

Section titled “Why thumbnails go blank”

Instagram serves media through CDN URLs that expire after a period. LinktoDM displays the URL Instagram gave it when the post was fetched; once that link lapses, the image stops loading while everything else about the post stays valid.

That’s why older automations lose their previews first, and why the picker often looks fine for recent posts and patchy further down.

Get the previews back

Section titled “Get the previews back”

Refresh the page. LinktoDM re-fetches the post list, Instagram issues fresh URLs, and the images return. This fixes most cases.

Check the post still exists. A post that was deleted or archived on Instagram has no thumbnail to serve — and unlike an expired URL, this one does matter: the automation attached to it can no longer trigger. Open the post on Instagram to confirm, and repoint the automation if it’s gone.

Reconnect if every thumbnail is blank. All previews missing across every account usually means the connection can’t read your media at all — refresh permissions via Instagram automation not working.

Try another browser. An ad blocker or strict tracking protection blocking Instagram’s CDN domain will hide thumbnails and nothing else. An incognito window tells you in seconds.

The one case that isn’t cosmetic

Section titled “The one case that isn’t cosmetic”

In a story automation, the story picker showing “No story · Add a story and try again” is not a loading failure — it means no story is currently live on the account. Instagram stories expire after 24 hours, and the picker only reads live ones. Post a story and reopen the picker, or point the automation at all stories or next story instead.

Check the trigger, not the picture

If an automation stopped working and its thumbnail is missing, the thumbnail isn’t the cause. Start at comment automation not working instead.
